CODE
Art. 2.3.46. 
Amount and proof of rewards 
Reward may not be less than the impoverishment of the creditor's patrimony. However, if the sums and funds entered into the debtor's patrimony have been used to acquire, conserve or improve an asset, the reward is equal to the value or increase in value acquired by that asset, either at the dissolution of the regime, if it is in the debtor's patrimony at that time, or on the date of its alienation if it has been alienated previously; if a new asset has replaced the alienated asset, the reward is assessed on the basis of the new asset.
The right to rewards is established by any means of proof.
 Rewards bear interest ipso jure from the date of dissolution of the regime.
